Let’s do a more targeted check. My ZIP code is 94103, my carrier is AT&T, and I’m using an iPhone 13 with iOS 17.5.1. I’m having trouble with both calls and data since this morning. No error messages, but my signal is very weak. Can you check for any issues in my area?

Thanks for the details. I ran a basic service status check and I’m not seeing a widespread outage flagged right now. That suggests it may be a localized issue in your part of 94103, building/indoor signal loss, or a line/device configuration issue.

Try these quick fixes first (in order):
- Toggle Airplane Mode for 30 seconds, then turn it off.
- Restart the iPhone (power off, wait 20 seconds, power on).
- Check for carrier settings update: Settings > General > About. If a prompt appears, accept it.
- Temporarily switch off 5G to see if LTE is steadier: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Voice & Data > choose LTE. Also try turning off “5G Auto” if it’s on.
- Turn Wi‑Fi Calling on (helps for weak indoor signal): Settings > Phone > Wi‑Fi Calling.
- If you use an eSIM: Settings > Cellular > toggle your line off, wait 15 seconds, then back on. If it’s a physical SIM: power off, reseat the SIM, power on.
- Reset Network Settings if issues persist: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. Note this erases saved Wi‑Fi/VPN settings.

Check location variables:
- Step outside or move near a window to see if signal and data improve.
- Walk a block or two to test if it’s location-specific. If it improves quickly, it’s likely local signal or congestion.

If problems continue after the above:
- Verify your account is in good standing and no blocks are on your line (AT&T can check and push a reprovision/refresh).
- Look for local outage notices: att.com/outages (enter 94103) or status.att.com, and optionally a third‑party tracker like Downdetector.
- If multiple AT&T users around you have the same issue, it strongly points to a local network problem—AT&T support can open a network ticket.

Quick questions to narrow it down:
- Are you using a physical SIM or eSIM on the iPhone 13?
- Does service improve outdoors or in another nearby spot?
- After switching to LTE only, do calls and data stabilize?

Tell me what you observe and I can suggest the next best step or help you contact AT&T with the right details.

I’m using a physical SIM. I tried stepping outside, but the signal is still weak and calls/data are unreliable. Switching to LTE only didn’t make a noticeable difference either. What should I do next?

Thanks for checking those. Since it’s still weak outdoors and LTE-only didn’t help, the next best steps are to isolate whether it’s the SIM/phone or the network in your immediate area.

Do these in order:
1) Reseat the SIM
- Power off the iPhone.
- Eject the SIM tray, remove the SIM, check for dust/damage, reinsert firmly, and power back on.
- Test calls and data.

2) Reset Network Settings
- Note: this will forget saved Wi‑Fi and VPN settings.
- Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings.
- After reboot, check for carrier settings update: Settings > General > About (accept if prompted).
- Re-test calls/data. Keep Data Mode on “Standard” and Voice & Data on LTE or 5G Auto.

3) Force a fresh network registration
- Settings > Cellular > Network Selection > turn off Automatic, wait 10–15 seconds for the list, then manually pick AT&T. If it fails, turn Automatic back on after 30 seconds and test again.

4) Use Wi‑Fi Calling as a workaround
- Settings > Phone > Wi‑Fi Calling > On. This can stabilize calls while we sort the cellular side.

5) Quick isolation test if possible
- Try your SIM in another AT&T‑compatible phone, or try a known‑good AT&T SIM in your iPhone 13.
- If your SIM works fine elsewhere, your iPhone may be at fault. If your iPhone works fine with another SIM, your SIM/account is likely the issue.

Optional but useful:
- Check for iOS and app updates: Settings > General > Software Update.
- If you use a VPN or have a device management profile, turn the VPN off and retry data (VPN won’t affect call signal, but it can affect data reliability).
- Field test (signal quality): Dial *3001#12345#* and press call. If you see LTE/NR RSRP worse than about −120 dBm or RSRQ worse than −15 dB consistently outdoors, that indicates very poor signal and likely a local network issue.

If it’s still unreliable after the above:
- Visit an AT&T store for a free SIM replacement (especially if your SIM is a few years old) and ask them to reprovision your line.
- Contact AT&T support to:
  - Refresh your network registration and VoLTE/IMS provisioning.
  - Check your account for any blocks.
  - Check for local tower maintenance/degradation and open a network ticket if needed.

What to provide AT&T to speed things up:
- Location: 94103, plus nearest cross streets or a specific address.
- Timeframe: started this morning; include 2–3 example times when calls/data failed.
- Device: iPhone 13, iOS 17.5.1, physical SIM; steps you’ve already tried (outdoor test, LTE-only, SIM reseat, network reset).
- Any field-test readings if you captured them.

Want me to stay on and walk you through the SIM reseat and network reset now? Also, do you have access to a second phone or a spare AT&T SIM for the quick swap test?
I’d appreciate step-by-step guidance for reseating the SIM and resetting network settings. I don’t have a spare phone or SIM available right now.

Great—here are clear, step-by-step instructions for both tasks. Take them in order. If anything looks different on your phone, tell me what you see.

Part 1: Reseat the physical SIM
- What you’ll need: SIM eject tool (from the iPhone box) or a small paperclip.
- Find the SIM tray: On iPhone 13, it’s on the left edge of the phone (when the screen faces you).
- Power off the iPhone: Press and hold the side button + a volume button > slide to power off. Wait 15 seconds.
- Eject the tray: Insert the SIM tool straight into the small pinhole next to the tray. Press gently until the tray pops out.
- Inspect and clean:
  - Lift the SIM out carefully. Avoid touching the gold contacts.
  - Check for dust/debris. If needed, wipe the SIM and tray lightly with a dry, lint-free cloth.
  - Check for damage: deep scratches, chips, or a bent tray. If damaged, plan to replace the SIM at an AT&T store.
- Reinsert correctly:
  - Align the SIM with the notch so it sits flat in the tray—don’t force it.
  - Slide the tray back in fully and flush with the phone.
- Power on and test:
  - Turn the phone back on.
  - Wait 1–2 minutes for signal bars to settle.
  - Test a call and try loading a web page with Wi‑Fi off.

If it’s still unreliable, proceed to Part 2.

Part 2: Reset Network Settings (this clears saved Wi‑Fi networks and VPN/APN settings)
- Make sure you know your Wi‑Fi password(s) before proceeding.
- Go to: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings.
- Enter your passcode and confirm. The phone will reboot automatically.
- After reboot:
  - Reconnect to Wi‑Fi (if desired).
  - Check for a carrier settings update: Settings > General > About, wait ~15 seconds. If a prompt appears, accept it.
  - Optional: Set Cellular options back to typical defaults:
    - Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options:
      - Voice & Data: 5G Auto (or LTE if you prefer)
      - Data Mode: Standard
  - Test again: turn Wi‑Fi off, try a call, then try loading a few websites/apps.

Optional immediate workaround
- Turn on Wi‑Fi Calling to stabilize calls while we troubleshoot: Settings > Phone > Wi‑Fi Calling > On, follow prompts.

What to tell me next
- After the SIM reseat: did the phone find signal quickly, and are calls/data any better?
- After the network reset: any change in bars, call reliability, or data speed?
- If it’s still poor, I’ll guide you through the next steps (manual network selection to force re-registration, then contacting AT&T for a SIM replacement and line reprovision).
I followed your instructions to reseat the SIM and reset the network settings. After rebooting, my signal bars are still low, and calls and data remain unreliable. What should I try next?

Thanks for sticking with it. Since the SIM reseat and network reset didn’t help, let’s (1) force a fresh network registration, (2) rule out easy external factors, (3) capture signal metrics, and (4) either swap the SIM/convert to eSIM or get AT&T to refresh your line and open a network ticket.

Do these in order:

1) Force fresh registration on AT&T
- Manual network selection:
  - Settings > Cellular > Network Selection > turn OFF Automatic.
  - Wait 10–20 seconds for networks to appear.
  - Tap AT&T. If it errors, wait 30 seconds and try once more.
  - Then turn Automatic back ON.
- Toggle your line:
  - Settings > Cellular > tap your line > turn off this line, wait 15–20 seconds, turn it back on.
- Quick radio refresh:
  - Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data > turn off for 30 seconds > turn on.

2) Rule out common blockers
- Remove your phone case and any magnetic/MagSafe accessories; test again outdoors.
- Turn off any VPN: Settings > VPN > Off. Also check Settings > General > VPN & Device Management and temporarily remove any configuration profiles unless required.
- Make sure Wi‑Fi Calling is ON (good temporary workaround for calls): Settings > Phone > Wi‑Fi Calling > On, and complete the prompts.

3) Capture quick signal metrics (helps decide device vs. network and is useful for AT&T)
- Field Test Mode:
  - Dial *3001#12345#* and press call.
  - For LTE: look for RSRP and RSRQ. For 5G/NR: look for RSRP/RSRQ/RS-SINR.
  - What to note outdoors:
    - LTE RSRP better than about −110 dBm and RSRQ better than −12 dB is usable; worse than −120 dBm or RSRQ worse than −15 dB is poor.
    - 5G/NR RSRP better than about −110 dBm and SINR above ~5 dB is usable; very negative SINR or RSRP below −120 dBm is poor.
- Walk a block or two and check again. If readings stay poor across multiple spots outdoors, that strongly suggests a local network/tower issue rather than your phone.

4) If still unreliable: choose one or both of these next actions

A) Replace the SIM or convert to eSIM (fast and often effective)
- Visit an AT&T store for a free physical SIM swap, or convert to eSIM (which refreshes provisioning).
- If you prefer doing it yourself and have Wi‑Fi:
  - On iPhone 13, check Settings > Cellular > Convert to eSIM (if that option is present, follow the prompts).
  - Or use the myAT&T app: Devices > Activate or switch device > eSIM.
- After SIM swap/eSIM conversion, restart the phone, then test.

B) Contact AT&T to refresh your line and check the local network
- Call from another phone or use AT&T chat; if calling from your iPhone, use Wi‑Fi Calling.
- Ask the agent to:
  - Confirm your line is fully provisioned for HD Voice/VoLTE and 5G/LTE.
  - Push a network registration refresh and reprovision your SIM/IMSI.
  - Check for tower maintenance/degradation affecting 94103 (share nearest cross streets).
  - Open a network trouble ticket if no known outage. Provide 2–3 example failure times.
- Provide this info to speed things up:
  - Location: ZIP 94103, plus nearest cross streets or a specific address.
  - Since when: this morning.
  - Device: iPhone 13, iOS 17.5.1, physical SIM.
  - Steps tried: reseat SIM, network reset, LTE-only test, outdoor test, manual network selection (if you performed it).
  - Field test readings (RSRP/RSRQ/SINR) if you captured them.

Optional quick checks while you prepare the above
- Software update: Settings > General > Software Update (install if available).
- Data roaming: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Data Roaming ON (won’t usually matter on AT&T domestically, but safe to try).
- Private Relay/VPN off for data testing: Settings > Your name > iCloud > Private Relay > Off (just for testing).

Tell me:
- What happened after the manual network selection and line toggle?
- Your field test readings outdoors (RSRP/RSRQ/SINR) and whether they change a block or two away.
Based on that, I’ll advise whether to prioritize the SIM swap/eSIM conversion or push AT&T to open a local network ticket.

I completed the manual network selection and toggled my line as you described, but the signal didn’t improve. I also checked the field test readings outdoors—my LTE RSRP is around −122 dBm and RSRQ is −16 dB, which seems pretty poor. The readings didn’t change much when I walked a block away. What do you recommend I do next?

Your field-test readings (RSRP ≈ −122 dBm, RSRQ ≈ −16 dB outdoors across multiple nearby spots) point to a local network/tower issue rather than your phone or SIM. Next steps that will actually move the needle:

Priority actions
1) Keep Wi‑Fi Calling on as a workaround
- This will stabilize calling and texting while the cellular issue is addressed.

2) Open a network trouble ticket with AT&T
- How to contact: dial 611 from your phone (use Wi‑Fi Calling), or call 800‑331‑0500, or start chat via the myAT&T app/att.com.
- What to say (copy/paste):
  “I’m experiencing persistently poor AT&T signal and unreliable calls/data outdoors in ZIP 94103 since this morning. Field-test shows LTE RSRP around −122 dBm and RSRQ −16 dB at multiple spots a block apart. I’ve reseated the SIM, reset network settings, tried LTE-only, manual network selection, and line toggling with no improvement. - Not likely to fix a weak RF signal, but it’s quick and removes SIM/account variables.
- Options:
  - Visit an AT&T store for a free SIM replacement and line reprovision.
  - Or convert to eSIM on your iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Convert to eSIM (if shown), then restart and test.

If the location is important (home/work)
- Ask AT&T about an AT&T Cell Booster (their LTE femtocell). It uses your internet to create strong indoor coverage at your address. This won’t fix outdoor coverage but can solve calls/data at home or the office while AT&T works on the tower.

While you pursue the ticket
- Leave Wi‑Fi Calling on.
- Keep VPN/Private Relay off when testing cellular data.
- If you notice a time-of-day pattern (for example, peak-hour congestion), note it for AT&T; it helps them prioritize capacity fixes.
